subject: SIG intake: PR lifecycle narratives, ephemeral token lineage & rollback choreography

Subject: SIG / CAIQ ask: PR lifecycle narratives + token lineage + rollback example

Marcus / team,

Thanks for taking this intake. As part of the SIG assessment for FinServCo we need: 

1) A short narrative (1-2 paragraphs) describing your PR review lifecycle and how code reviews are sampled for assessor validation.
2) An audit sample showing ephemeral token lineage for CI agents (creation -> use -> expiry/rotation) for three sample runs. CSV or log extract is fine (redact PII).
3) A single-page diagram or a short written choreography detailing an emergency rollback/hotfix sequence (who authorizes, how the rollback is triggered, how secrets are handled during rollback).

Deadline: can you provide the artifacts by COB Thursday (2028-10-25)? If you have existing links or a drive folder, pointing us there is fine.

Attachments requested (optional): sampling manifest, pipeline snippets, lineage extract, rollback runbook.

Regards,
Leah Monroe
Senior Assessor, SecurityAssess Inc.

Marcus / Leah,

Quick tech note on the token lineage ask: we extract ephemeral token lifecycle from our CI audit stream. For the sample I prepared a redacted CSV with the following columns: run_id, agent_id, token_issued_at, token_expiry_at, rotation_event_id, user_trigger (if any). I have attached two small snippets of the pipeline job that record token mint/rotate events (ci-pipeline-snippets.txt) and a sampling manifest describing the PR selection criteria (pr-sampling-manifest.md).

Our default practice:
- CI agents request tokens scoped to a short TTL (default 15m) via ephemeral credential service.
- Tokens are tied to run_id and stored only in ephemeral in-memory contexts; audit entries are emitted to the pipeline audit topic and archived for 90 days.
- Rotations are automatic on a retry count or explicit rotation call by the runner.

I redacted user emails in the sample. If you need hashed identifiers instead of redaction for linkage, let me know.

Attachments: ci-pipeline-snippets.txt, pr-sampling-manifest.md

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — the plan sounds good. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For the token lineage sample we prefer a minimal set of three runs that include an explicit rotation event mid-run (if available), so we can validate the event chain.
2) For the rollback choreography, the assessor prefers a realistic sequence with timestamps and the specific policy used to escalate an emergency rollback (e.g., severity thresholds, who authorizes bypass). A short PDF or one-page diagram is ideal.

If you can place the items in the Drive folder by Thurs 5pm PT that will be perfect.

-Leah

Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ ask: PR lifecycle narratives + token lineage + rollback example

Leah — attaching the final items per your asks. Links below are live to the redacted artifacts in the assessor folder. Summary of what's provided: 

- PR lifecycle narrative (short): describes required reviewers, automated checks, merge gating, and the sampling approach used for assessor review. See Drive > PR Narrative (one paragraph + checklist).
- pr-sampling-manifest.md (attached): describes how we select PRs (random stratified sampling by service, size, and risk tag).
- ci-pipeline-snippets.txt (attached): redacted snippets that show where tokens are minted and rotation events emitted.
- token-lineage-audit.csv (attached): three sample runs (run_20280819_003, run_20280902_011, run_20281012_002) with rotation anchors included. Redacted columns: user_email replaced with hashed_user_id.
- rollback-choreography.pdf (attached): one-page sequence diagram with timestamps, triggers, and authorization flow. It documents the emergency rollback path and explains how secrets are temporarily handled (on-call rotates short-lived secret bridge; rollback uses allowlisted service accounts that require two-person authorization via PagerDuty acceptance + Ops lead sign-off).

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A7nXq_example_folder
Jira : https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SIG-8920

Notes / Controls: we retain audit stream for 90 days; rotation events are immutable in the archive. If the assessor needs longer retention slices for regulatory review, we can produce encrypted exports under a data sharing agreement.

Attachments: ci-pipeline-snippets.txt, pr-sampling-manifest.md, token-lineage-audit.csv, rollback-choreography.pdf

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
